- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overreaction.  
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model often underestimates rebound; increase forecast mid-range by 2–5% to capture momentum.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to lag behind true trend; add 1–2 days of lagged price adjustment to align with actual momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period volatility; increase forecast variance in final 5–7 days if sentiment is volatile or bullish.
